subject: Follow-up: Dedicated fit — concurrency & token mix confirmation
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@orbithealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated fit — concurrency & token mix confirmation

Sam — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and the key asks we agreed to close to determine a Dedicated recommendation:

- Deployment mode: leaning Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) but evaluating whether Private VPC is required for you. You indicated US-only data residency.
- Sizing inputs we need from you:
  • Sustained TPS target (requests/sec)
  • Peak/burst TPS and expected burst duration
  • Typical token mix: average prompt tokens / average generation tokens, percent of short vs long completions
  • Percent of requests that are chat-style (multi-turn) vs single-shot completions vs embeddings/reranking
  • Latency SLOs (p50/p95) and any tail constraints
  • Any hard constraints: on-prem requirement, air-gapped, specific GPU family preference

I've attached the dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx to capture these. If you can populate and return by EOD Thursday (2027-01-14) we'll run a quick capacity model and propose two SKU options (A100 80GB vs H100) with concurrency knobs and cost estimates.

Next steps
- Sam: confirm the bullets above and attach any traffic samples / token-distribution CSV
- Karthik / Vanessa: I'll loop you in for a technical sizing call after we get the template back

Thanks,

Evelyn Hart
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@orbithealth.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated fit — concurrency & token mix confirmation

Thanks, Sam / Evelyn — two quick clarifying items from the runtime side to help us model throughput:

1) Tokenization: are you using a standard tokenizer (e.g., GPT-style) or a custom pre-tokenization? If custom, please include a sample prompt so we can estimate tokenization ratio.
2) Typical request shapes:
   - Short queries: <= 64 prompt tokens / <= 32 generation tokens
   - Mid queries: 200–600 prompt tokens / 80–300 generation tokens
   - Long summaries: > 1500 tokens total
Please indicate approximate % of traffic in those buckets.

Suggested modeling options we'll run once we have inputs:
- A100 80GB (trimmed KV cache concurrency) — better for stable sustained throughput
- H100 80GB (fp8/quant path) — better peak TPS with lower per-token cost but requires quantization testing
- Mixed pool (H100 for short, A100 for long sequences) — can optimize cost/latency mix

I'll also prepare a quick concurrency table (tokens in KV per concurrent request vs GPU memory) for the workshop.

—Karthik
Principal Systems Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@orbithealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 08:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated fit — concurrency & token mix confirmation

Thanks — see answers below and attached traffic_sample_q1.csv:

- Sustained TPS: 250 RPS (mostly inference calls for patient-summary generation)
- Peak/burst TPS: we see spikes up to ~900 RPS for 60–180s during batch processing windows and morning syncs
- Token mix (approx):
  • Average prompt tokens: 450
  • Average generated tokens: 120
  • Distribution: 55% chat completions (multi-turn), 25% single-shot completions, 20% embedding/rerank batches
- Tokenization: standard GPT-style tokenizer (we're using the open tokenizer)
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 250 ms for short queries (<200 tokens); for long/summary requests we can accept p95 <= 1200 ms
- Residency: US only
- Procurement timeline: decision by end of Q1; pilot in Feb if sizing looks good

Attachments: traffic_sample_q1.csv (csv), network_requirements_draft.pdf (pdf)

Happy to jump on the sizing workshop — mornings PT tend to work best for our infra team.

Sam Lee
Head of ML Eng | OrbitHealth

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@orbithealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated fit — concurrency & token mix confirmation

Great — appreciate the fast turnaround and the sample.

Preliminary recommendation (based on your sustained + burst pattern and token mix):

Option A (cost-conscious): 6x A100 80GB nodes with steady concurrency of 40–60 per GPU, optimized KV cache for long summaries. Expected sustained handling ~250 RPS with p95 ~180–220ms for short queries; burst handling with autoscaled burst pool to ~600 RPS.

Option B (performance + burst): 4x H100 80GB nodes with mixed-precision quant path for short chats and an A100-style fallback for long sequences. Expected sustained handling ~250 RPS with higher burst headroom to ~900 RPS with p95 ~150–250ms.

We recommend we run a sizing workshop next week to validate memory/concurrency with your traffic_sample_q1.csv. Proposed times (PT):
- Thu Jan 14, 09:00–10:00
- Fri Jan 15, 10:00–11:00

Action items
- Sam: confirm preferred slot and whether you want us to include a short quantization test in the pilot
- Karthik/Vanessa: I'll book a 60-min workshop and share a post-workshop sizing readout + pricing estimate

Links: HubSpot deal ORB-2027-042 (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ORB-2027-042), Sizing template (drive link: https://drive.google.com/sample-link)

Thanks,

Evelyn Hart
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
